BACKGROUND

A little background

The title track of Lang Lee’s third album features Unnie Choir, which the official album notes describe as a group celebrating sexual diversity and feminism. The album was released on August 23, 2021; the featured video is a later live performance.

INSIDE THE LYRICS

Who gets called a wolf

  • Poverty
  • Exclusion
  • Labour

The closed city gates separate hungry people from the food kept within. As people grieve, demand bread or take grain, threatening labels follow them. The wolf of the title can be read as a name imposed on people whose hunger is treated as a danger, while the conditions behind their actions go unanswered.

Later, the people being described speak for themselves. They identify themselves as the makers of bread and wine, insisting on their work and their need to feed their children. The speaker’s reference to poor friends also brings the story closer to everyday life. Poverty becomes something the addressee is asked to consider as a possible part of their own future.

ABOUT THE ARTIST / 이랑

Lang Lee

Lang Lee writes songs about poverty, loss and the lives of people around her. Her collaborations with Unnie Choir bring a collective voice to songs about exclusion and separation.

She released her third album, There is A Wolf, on August 23, 2021. She wrote all ten songs and arranged and produced the album with De-bong Lee.
